tavily.text:
To set up the PR Agent Python project, first, acquire the App private key and App ID from your app's settings page. Clone the repository using `git clone`. Then, copy the secrets template file and fill in the required information. Set the `PYTHONPATH` to include your `pr-agent` project directory using either Option A by adding `PYTHONPATH="/PATH/TO/PROJECTS/pr-agent` to your `.env` file or Option B by setting `PYTHONPATH` and running the CLI in one command. Install dependencies using `uv sync` from `uv.lock` and run tests with `PYTHONPATH=.` set. Secrets should be supplied through environment variables, not persisted in code or configuration files. Adjust runtime behavior by overriding keys in `.pr_agent.toml` or by supplying repository-specific Dynaconf files.
To install the PR Agent Python documentation, first, acquire the necessary information from your app's settings page, including the App private key, App ID. Clone the repository using `git clone`. Then, copy the secrets template file and fill in the required details. Set the `PYTHONPATH` to include your `pr-agent` project directory using either Option A by adding `PYTHONPATH="/PATH/TO/PROJECTS/pr-agent` to your `.env` file or Option B by setting `PYTHONPATH` and running the CLI in one command. Install dependencies with `uv sync` and run tests with `PYTHONPATH=.` set to keep imports functional. Adjust configuration through `.pr_agent.toml` or files under `pr_agent/settings/` instead of hard-coding values.
To install the pr-agent Python package, you can use pip to download version 0.2.7 from PyPI. The installation command is `pip install pr-agent==0.2.7`. The pr-agent package aims to help efficiently review and handle pull requests by providing AI feedbacks and suggestions. It includes tools like `/improve` for code suggestions, `/analyze` for identifying changed code components, and `/custom_prompt` for generating custom suggestions based on specific guidelines. The package also supports adjusting the response language and has been updated to address community-identified vulnerabilities.
